events.title: The election of Pope Adrian VI
events.shortBlurb: The cardinals unexpectedly chose a Dutch reformer, the last non-Italian pope until the twentieth century…
body: On 9 January 1522 a conclave deadlocked among its factions unexpectedly elected, in his absence, Adrian Florensz Boeyens, born at Utrecht in 1459, a former professor at Louvain who had been tutor to the young Charles V and was then governing Spain as the emperor's regent.

He took the name Adrian VI and remains the only Dutchman to sit on the throne of Peter. Reaching Rome only in August 1522, an austere stranger to its court, he set about cutting its expenses and, through his legate at the Diet of Nuremberg, confessed that the evils afflicting the Church had spread from the Roman see itself.

His earnest reform met resistance on every side, and his reign lasted scarcely twenty months: he died on 14 September 1523 and was buried in the German church of Santa Maria dell'Anima. After him no non-Italian was elected pope until John Paul II in 1978.
